title: Tide Business Bank
intro: Tide is a simple online business banking service made for small businesses and freelancers, helping you manage your money easily through its smart and easy-to-use app.
body: Tide is a UK-based fintech platform that provides business banking accounts and financial tools for small businesses, freelancers and sole traders.
It’s important to note that Tide **isn’t a full bank with its own banking licence** — instead it works with a partner bank (ClearBank) so your money is held securely via their infrastructure.
You can open an account online in minutes, manage your expenses, send invoices and connect accounting software.
Speed & convenience: You can open a business account quickly via the app, with less paperwork than many traditional banks.
Useful business tools: For small businesses, Tide offers things like invoicing, tracking expenses, and linking to accounting software — helping you save time.
Low/transparent fees: Depending on your plan, it can cost less than many traditional business bank accounts — good for freelancers or smaller firms.
Security & regulation: Although not a bank in the strictest sense, your funds are held via ClearBank and regulations are in place to protect your account.
**Why choose us (if you’re using our recommendation)?**
If you’re a small business owner, freelancer or startup in the UK and you want banking that:
Is mobile-friendly and digital (you manage it mostly via app),
Understands the needs of smaller businesses (invoicing, bookkeeping, easy transfers).

has relatively simple pricing and fewer legacy banking headaches — then Tide is a strong choice in that niche. We’re recommending it because it matches the “modern business” style rather than old‐school branch-based banking.
Since it’s app-based and digital-first, customer service may differ from high street banks (less branch availability, heavy reliance on chat/support rather than in-person).
Because it’s technically not a fully licensed bank on its own, there may be extra checks or limitations (e.g., deposit options, cash services) compared to a full bank.
As with any account for business use, make sure your business activities, income flows etc match what the provider expects — there may be more scrutiny.
